questions.prompt: What is a 'day' on a planet?
options: One full rotation of the planet around its own axis
One full orbit around the Sun
questions.explanation: A day is one complete spin of the planet around its axis. Earth spins once every 24 hours, so our day is 24 hours.
questions.misconception: 'Day' and 'year' get swapped often: a year is one orbit of the Sun, a day is one spin of the planet — two completely different motions.

questions.prompt: Which planet has the shortest day of all?
questions.explanation: Jupiter spins faster than any other planet — one rotation takes only about 9.9 hours, so its day is the shortest.
questions.misconception: It feels natural for the biggest planet to spin slowly, but Jupiter is actually the solar system's fastest spinner.

questions.prompt: What is unusual about the way Venus rotates?
options: It spins backwards compared with most planets (retrograde)
Its rotation axis lies exactly on its orbit
questions.explanation: Venus spins in the opposite direction from Earth and most other planets, so on Venus the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
questions.misconception: Since Venus is sometimes called Earth's twin (similar size), it is easy to assume its spin is like Earth's — but its direction is actually reversed.

questions.prompt: How does a Mars day compare with an Earth day?
options: Mars has no day at all
questions.explanation: Mars rotates nearly as fast as Earth — one Mars day is about 24.6 hours, just under 40 minutes longer than ours.
questions.misconception: Since Mars's year is about twice Earth's, it feels like its day should also be longer — but day length is about spin, and Mars's spin is nearly identical to Earth's.

questions.prompt: What is strange about Mercury's day compared with its year?
options: Its day is longer than its year
Its day is exactly equal to its year
Its day is one week long
There is no day on Mercury
questions.explanation: Mercury rotates very slowly — one of its days lasts about 176 Earth days, while its year is only 88 Earth days. Its day is twice its year.
questions.misconception: A day shorter than a year seems so universal (it's true on Earth) that it feels like a universal rule — Mercury breaks it, which is exactly why its day/night cycle is so extreme.
